Vendored-source change 3 to ShadowHook 2.0.1
============================================

File: shadowhook/src/main/cpp/common/sh_trampo.c, in sh_trampo_alloc_between.

The reuse scan is skipped, so every trampoline allocation gets its own fresh
mmap'd page instead of taking the next free slot in an existing one.

Why
---
Reusing a slot in a page that already holds a live trampoline faults on this
device. Instrumenting the allocator showed it precisely:

  trampo: NEW   page=7b0c786000 len=4096, zeroing      -> ok, slot 0
  trampo: REUSE page=7b0c786000 slot=1 trampo=...100   -> ok
  trampo: REUSE page=7b0c786000 slot=2 trampo=...200   -> SIGSEGV, SEGV_ACCERR

The page is mapped PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC and was zeroed in full when
it was created, and /proc/self/maps confirms rwxp at that moment. Yet a later
256 byte write at offset 0x200 takes an access violation, while offsets 0 and
0x100 were written successfully just before.

What distinguishes the failing write is that trampolines in the earlier slots
have been executed by then. The behaviour is consistent with this kernel
revoking write access to an anonymous RWX page once instructions have been
fetched from it, which is a reasonable W^X hardening measure and is invisible
in the maps output. A standalone probe inside the same process, mapping RWX and
writing the whole page and then offset 0x200, succeeds every time, which fits:
nothing has executed from that page.

Not reproducible from outside, and not something the engine can detect, so the
allocation strategy is changed instead.

Cost
----
One page per hook. This project installs 18, so 72 KB. The reuse scan existed
to amortise that, and nothing else depends on it.
